headline: Last coffee sale of the season averaged Sh38,140 per 50-kg bag
summary: That is about Sh117 per kg of cherry before milling, marketing and other deductions. The new coffee year began on 1 October.
source: Kenya News Agency (Nairobi Coffee Exchange results)

headline: Above-average rain forecast for coffee counties in October
summary: KMD expects above-average rain in Nyeri, Kirinyaga, Murang'a, Kiambu, Embu and Meru this month, with heavy falls in several places. September was mostly dry.
dateNote: Date is the issue date printed on the forecast PDF (30th September 2026); the web page itself shows only the validity period 1-31 Oct 2026.

headline: Wet El Nino weather raises fungal disease risk: check plants often
summary: Long wet spells and high humidity favour fungal diseases. Inspect plants regularly for early signs of infection and stay alert for pests such as armyworm and locusts.
source: aak-GROW / CropLife Kenya (reported by The Star)
dateNote: Industry advice reported by a newspaper, not a government notice; the article does not mention coffee by name.

headline: Researchers screening new coffee crosses for disease resistance
summary: Kalro's Coffee Research Institute is screening new Arabica-Robusta crosses. Of today's varieties, Ruiru 11 and Batian offer the strongest disease resistance.
source: KALRO Coffee Research Institute (reported by The Star)
dateNote: Research news reported by a newspaper quoting a Coffee Research Institute scientist; no new variety is released yet.

headline: Short rains start mid-October and look wetter than normal
summary: KMD expects rain in Nyeri, Kirinyaga, Murang'a, Kiambu, Meru and Embu from the 2nd-3rd week of October, continuing into January, with above-average totals.
dateNote: Date is the issue date printed on the NCOF13 statement PDF (26th Aug 2026); the web page shows only the season dates.

headline: Spray copper fungicide before the rains to curb coffee berry disease
summary: A Coffee Research Institute pathologist says berry disease thrives in cool, wet weather. Use copper sprays before the rains at the right dose, and prune to open the canopy.
source: KALRO Coffee Research Institute (reported by Kenya News Agency)
dateNote: Older than the other items (about 18 months) but the advice applies to the coming short rains. Spoken at a Murang'a farmers' open day.
